neighbours.label: something being given up or surrendered in exchange for something else (the thing traded away in a 'surrender X in exchange for Y' bargain); the same nouns held or used without being traded away stay low
fire: In the deal, the rebels agreed to surrender their weapons in exchange for an amnesty.
Many employees accept lower salaries in exchange for the freedom to work from home.
Under the settlement, the company will relinquish its patents in return for a cash payment.
Early settlers were asked to forfeit their hunting rights in exchange for farmland.
Each member state cedes some sovereignty in return for access to the common market.
The prisoner offered to give up the names of his partners in exchange for a shorter sentence.
Some travellers trade away their privacy in exchange for faster airport security checks.
The club sacrificed its youngest striker in return for two experienced defenders.
quiet: In the deal, the rebels were allowed to keep their weapons while the talks continued.
Many employees enjoy higher salaries and the freedom to work from home.
Under the settlement, the company will continue to license its patents to partners.
Early settlers kept their hunting rights and also cleared new farmland.
Each member state keeps its own sovereignty over taxes and defence.
The prisoner refused to say anything at all during the long interview.
Some travellers value their privacy and avoid posting photos online.
The club signed its youngest striker to a new five-year contract.
